overview: This table matches each line of dialogue in the downloadable story with the voice that speaks it.
description: Maps DLC story-demo message/text IDs to the VoiceDataTable row whose cue is spoken with the displayed message; two numbered table shards share FGameDataTableRow_DlcStoryDemoVoice.

Id.simple: The line of dialogue shown on screen in the downloadable story. Change this name to connect the entry to a different line.
Id.technical: FName row/import key (export field ID; Properties.ImportKeyField = Id; the empty constructor leaves the FName default NAME_None). Show-message commands take the current message ID from the script's sorted text-ID list and ParseVoice compares it with Row->Id across DTM.DlcStoryDemoVoiceDataTables; level-sequence sections pass their TextId directly. Script preload instead loops the discovered, unsorted message IDs and takes the first matching row in table order (shard 1 before shard 2). Those IDs come from AGameTextManager::FindTextIdsContaining on the story-text prefix derived by GameScript_GetStoryTextId (A -> 01 and B -> 03 for non-short stories), so the key is a localized text ID, not necessarily the raw script asset name. Both exports have non-empty, unique keys with no duplicates within or across shards.

Id_Voice.simple: The spoken voice that plays with that line of dialogue. Change this name to use a different voice recording, and leave it empty when the line should have no voice.
Id_Voice.technical: FName at row offset +0x10 (header Id_Voice; export field Id_Voice; default NAME_None). ParseVoice resolves it with GameScript_FindVoiceRow(VoiceDataTables, Id_Voice, false, false), so the first Voice table holding that row wins; on success it queues VoiceRow->CueSheetName/CueName with Delay = GetMessageTime(TimeId) and the line's Slot (0-3). TimeId TEXT_TIME_NONE skips parsing entirely, numeric time names are Atof seconds, and unmapped names resolve to 0.0f; a missing Voice row queues no voice. Script preload performs the same join but only takes CueSheetName and moves to the next message ID when no Voice row resolves. The level-sequence evaluator does not pre-resolve the row: it copies Id_Voice into VoiceId (a DLC row overwrites the standard row), skips None or already-requested playback, and UAbramsSequencerSoundModule::PlayVoice then resolves the ID through FindSoundRow(2, VoiceId) to VoiceDataTables before playing CueSheetName/CueName at volume 1.0. All 1,063 exported Id_Voice values are non-empty, unique Vo<ID> strings, and every one resolves in VoiceDataTable with non-empty cue fields; CueName equals the Voice ID in every case.

notes: Loading and precedence: GameDataTableManager registers the primary assets DlcStoryDemoVoiceDataTable1 and DlcStoryDemoVoiceDataTable2 (lines 423-424), waits for all table loaders, then appends the resolved non-null UDataTable pointers in that order to DTM.DlcStoryDemoVoiceDataTables (+0x790). FGameDataTableArray::GetRows walks table order then row-name order, and every consumer uses the combined array, so a duplicate ID would resolve from shard 1 first. The companion exports are disjoint: 200 keys in shard 1 and 863 in shard 2 (1,063 total), both with RowStruct GameDataTableRow_DlcStoryDemoVoice.

Selection differs by consumer. ParseVoice checks GameScript_IsDlcScript first (a Script row plus the matching StoryDemo row's chapter flag, not an ID prefix) and only then its STDM_SS_ short-story branch. Cue-sheet preload checks GALLERY_ first, then GameScript_IsSubStoryScript (fixed 'Part' cue sheet), then GameScript_IsDlcScript, then the standard table; a script name that qualifies as both substory and DLC therefore uses different mappings in those two consumers. The level-sequence path ignores script classification: it checks the standard table first, then the DLC table, and the DLC Id_Voice overwrites the standard one, including overwriting it with NAME_None.

There are no numeric or array fields in this row. Voice delay and slot come from the ShowMessage command's TimeId and line index; TEXT_TIME_NONE suppresses ParseVoice, numeric TimeIds are seconds, and an unmapped name gives 0.0f. The sequencer path uses volume 1.0f and is blocked when SoundModule->IsPlayRequested() is already true. No sentinel values are stored in the exported rows; both fields are non-empty and the constructor supplies only the FName default NAME_None.

Data relationships: message IDs are discovered from localized DLC GameText rows containing the rewritten story-text prefix; every exported DLC voice key also occurs in the DlcStoryDemoText shard exports, and every Id_Voice resolves in VoiceDataTable to the cue sheet and cue used by both script and sequencer playback. No DLC-row alias map or per-row cache was found: consumers re-walk the cached DTM table array, while the script player keeps only the resulting cue sheet name in CueSheetNames.

Evidence strength: reconstructed retail C++ with RVA provenance. status/functions.json records ParseVoice 0x14452a0, GameScript_IsDlcScript 0x1441710, sequencer PlayMessageVoice 0x179eff0, GetMessageTime 0x1436870 and SoundModule PlayVoice 0x17b2bb0 as byte-matched, while UpdateLoad 0x1440570, GameScript_FindVoiceRow 0x143b100, DTM Tick 0x13215c0 and SoundModule FindSoundRow 0x17aa520 are behaviour-certified. No retail Blueprint bytecode or live retail trace was inspected; no Blueprint-only behavior is claimed. Companion exports are available content, not a retail completeness claim.

usages.detail: Registers the first DLC voice primary-asset loader; line 424 registers the second.
Appends both resolved shards, in order, to DTM.DlcStoryDemoVoiceDataTables (+0x790).
Combined row collection preserves table order then row-name order, establishing shard 1 duplicate-key precedence.
ParseVoice selects this table for DLC scripts before checking the short-story branch.
Finds the first row in the combined shards whose Id equals the current message ID.
Resolves Id_Voice in VoiceDataTable and queues the cue sheet, cue, script time delay and voice slot.
Supplies the script's message IDs by scanning localized DLC GameText rows for the story-text prefix.
DLC cue-sheet preload walks discovered message IDs and uses the first DLC row whose Id_Voice resolves.
Looks up the section TextId after the standard table; a DLC hit overwrites VoiceId with Id_Voice.
Resolves the sequencer's VoiceId through VoiceDataTables (FindSoundRow kind 2) before playing the cue.
